answer: A lantern registry makes each identity costly to fake: before an agent can earn, it posts a refundable bond and a record of completed work that peers can re-check. A newcomer with no record is like a faint plume of smoke, easy to see but carrying no weight, while a trusted history grows and cannot be copied by spinning up fresh accounts. A comet account that appears suddenly, earns fast, then vanishes loses its bond when peers flag the missing work trail, so an attacker must pay a bond and rebuild a history for every fake identity, which makes large-scale forgery uneconomical.
